title: Analyzing and Evaluating Correlation Measures in NLG Meta-Evaluation

model.params_source: paper Sec. 3.2 (setting GPT4_T=0_1_5: temperature 0, one sample, scale 1-5); version by the date rule

task.subset_rule: all 30 meta-evaluation subsets D1-D30 (Table 4): SummEval 16x100x4, WMT23 zh-en news 16x376, HANNA 6x60x6, MANS 2x5x200, USR 2x5x60x6, WebNLG2020 16x178x5 (system, input, aspect) scorings
task.approximation: Aspect definitions are taken from the original datasets or were composed by the authors (Appendix B.2, not printed); {task}, {source_des}, {target_des} wordings not printed; r is an estimated parameter averaged over datasets, not a plain pooled correlation.

items.source: SummEval (github.com/Yale-LILY/SummEval), WMT23 ZH-EN news (mt-metrics-eval), HANNA, MANS (OpenMEVA), USR (Persona-Chat / Topical-Chat), WebNLG2020 human evaluation; the authors' data.csv (Google Drive link in github.com/kite99520/NLGCorrEval) holds scores only

fields.input: source text + system output per (system, input)
fields.label: human score per aspect

prompt.user_template:
###Instruction###
Please act as an impartial and helpful evaluator for natural language generation (NLG), and the audience is an expert in the field.
Your task is to evaluate the quality of {task} strictly based on the given evaluation criterion.
Begin the evaluation by providing your analysis concisely and accurately, and then on the next line, start with "Rating:" followed by your rating on a Likert scale from {scale} (higher means better).
You MUST keep to the strict boundaries of the evaluation criterion and focus solely on the issues and errors involved; otherwise, you will be penalized.
Make sure you read and understand these instructions, as well as the following evaluation criterion and example content, carefully.
###Evaluation Criterion###
{aspect}
###Example###
{source_des}:
{source}
{target_des}:
{target}
###Your Evaluation###

placeholders.aspect: aspect definition (original dataset or authors' wording, not printed)

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: Table 5 column r: Pearson correlation between metric and human scores under global grouping, estimated per meta-evaluation dataset after 0-1 normalization (Appendix C.2) and averaged over D1-D30; confirm against Sec. 2 (r_NxM = 0.51 is the alternative column)

open_points: The 30 meta-evaluation subsets (texts + human scores) must be assembled from six source datasets (SummEval, WMT23 zh-en, HANNA, MANS, USR, WebNLG2020); the released data.csv holds scores only.
Aspect definitions and the {task}/{source_des}/{target_des} wordings are not printed.
Confirm the definition of the r column (estimated global Pearson parameter) before comparing; a per-dataset comparison is not possible (Figure 4 only).
notes: Code repo github.com/kite99520/NLGCorrEval exists; 34,416 short calls at ~$0.01 each. || [hook pass 2026-09-07] no hook: inputs must be assembled from six external datasets with unprinted slot wordings.
